clue.text: Production of Ant and Dec's about sod all: "Electronic Story"

indicators.note: a production makes something new out of raw material, so the letters before it are worked into a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written; Ant and Dec are a British TV presenting duo
sod all is slang for nothing, which is the letter O
E is the standard abbreviation for electronic

explanation.surface: A sneer at a TV double act's latest show, which is said to be about nothing at all.
explanation.walkthrough: Ant and Dec (Anthony McPartlin and Declan Donnelly) present light entertainment on British TV. Their names plus the O for nothing are shuffled, and the E for electronic comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: An anecdote is a short personal story told for amusement, so it is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Try having a whopper as a player

blocks.note: to have a go is to try
taken as written
a whopper is a big lie

explanation.surface: Someone tries out for a team by telling a huge fib about their ability.
explanation.definitionFit: A goalie is the goalkeeper, one particular member of a team, so player is a broader term for it.

clue.text: Woman entertainer Harris mounted – awful scene (topless)

indicators.note: in a down entry, something mounted goes upward, so the name is read from bottom to top
without its top means the opening letter of the following word is removed
something awful is in a bad state, so the remaining letters are jumbled

blocks.note: Rolf Harris was an entertainer later convicted of sexual offences
taken as written before its first letter is lost

explanation.surface: A satirical jab: a woman mounted by a disgraced entertainer in a lurid scene with no top on.
explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye delights in this kind of scandal-flavoured surface. Ignore the brackets: topless strips the S from scene before the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Florence is a girl's given name, so it is an example of a woman's name, as crosswords often clue it.

clue.text: Mark: murders on the rise

indicators.note: something rising in a down entry travels upward, so the word is read bottom to top

blocks.note: to top someone is slang for to kill them

explanation.surface: A news-desk note that the murder rate is climbing.
explanation.definitionFit: A spot is a small mark or blemish, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Spot solicitor getting member to lose lots of money

indicators.note: losing something means it is taken away, here the abbreviation for a large sum

a leg is a limb, a member of the body
G stands for a grand, a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: A lawyer acquires a new member of the firm and forfeits a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: Solicitor looks like the British word for a lawyer, but it is one who solicits on the street.
explanation.definitionFit: A spot and a pimple are both small skin blemishes, so the words are synonyms.

clue.text: Bag attaching support to rugby players

blocks.note: to back someone is to support them
the pack is the group of forwards in a rugby team

explanation.surface: Someone fixes a kit bag on behind a set of rugby players.
explanation.definitionFit: A backpack is a rucksack, a kind of bag worn on the shoulders.

clue.text: Protrusion of organ gets the woman in a tizzy

blocks.note: her is the pronoun for the woman
taken as written before being shuffled

explanation.surface: A woman is thrown into a panic by a bulging organ.
explanation.walkthrough: In a looks like part of the phrase in a tizzy, but those two words are the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A hernia is where an internal organ pushes through the wall that should contain it, which is what protrusion describes.

clue.text: Start of unlikely colon replacement (not hip)

blocks.note: the opening letter of unlikely
taken as written before rearrangement

explanation.surface: A medical note that a colon transplant is improbable and, besides, unfashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: To be hip is to be fashionable and cool, so something not hip is unfashionable.

clue.text: They serve as genitalia

blocks.note: first meaning: soldiers of the lowest rank, who serve in the army
second meaning: a euphemism for the sexual organs

explanation.surface: A smutty remark about which body parts perform a service.
explanation.definitionFit: Privates are both army soldiers of the lowest rank and a coy word for the sex organs.

clue.text: Who to blame for Conservative rip-off concealed in last month

indicators.note: something gone off has gone wrong, so the word before it is rearranged

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
taken as written before rearrangement
ult., short for ultimo, means last month in formal letters

explanation.surface: Someone asks who is responsible for a Tory scam hushed up a month ago.
explanation.walkthrough: Rip-off reads as one word meaning a swindle, but it splits into a word and its shuffle signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A culprit is the person responsible for a crime or fault, the one people blame.

clue.text: (&24dn/12ac.) Screwing with Eye reader's organ, Cyclops gets name for meddling

blocks.note: poking is vulgar slang for having sex
a reader of Private Eye is addressed as you, so what belongs to them is yours
the nose is an organ of smell
Cyclops, the setter, refers to himself as I
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A smutty tale of a sexual encounter involving a reader's body part, for which the setter is blamed.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket at the start just links the three grid lights. The setter's pseudonym Cyclops stands for the first person, I.
explanation.definitionFit: Poking your nose in is an idiom for interfering in other people's business, which is meddling.

clue.text: see 11ac.
Labour could be so described: awfully lean party lacking finishing touch

done awfully means done badly, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written before its last letter goes

explanation.surface: A political jibe that the Labour Party is thin and unfinished.
explanation.walkthrough: Labour looks like the political party, but here it means childbirth.
explanation.definitionFit: Labour, the process of giving birth, takes place before a baby is born, so it is prenatal in the literal sense.

clue.text: Is sick of Penny on "the nation and drugs"

blocks.note: P is the abbreviation for a penny
the United Kingdom, the nation the magazine writes about
E is ecstasy, so drugs in the plural are Es

explanation.surface: Someone is fed up with a commentator called Penny banging on about the state of the nation and drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: To puke is slang for to vomit, so pukes means is sick.

clue.text: (& 16dn.) Do some personal shopping (á la Brenda) at M&S, say, with a nitwit's mad panic?

annotation.answer: GET ONE'S KNICKERS IN A TWIST

indicators.note: mad means crazed, so the letters of the phrase before it are scrambled

blocks.clueFragment: Do some personal shopping (á la Brenda) at M&S, say
blocks.note: Brenda is Private Eye's nickname for the late Queen, who says one for I, and M&S (Marks and Spencer) is the British store famous for underwear
taken as written
the possessive ending supplies the last letter of fodder

explanation.surface: The Queen buying her underwear at Marks and Spencer alongside a frantic idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: The first part describes the Queen's style of shopping for underwear in her royal one; nitwit's, including its S, is the rearranged part. Only panic defines the whole.
explanation.definitionFit: To get your knickers in a twist is a British idiom for getting flustered or agitated over something minor.

clue.text: Bad taste section not seen by audience

blocks.note: food that has gone off is bad and tastes off
a stage is a section of a journey or process

explanation.definitionFit: What happens offstage happens out of the audience's sight, beyond the visible area of a theatre.

clue.text: see 14ac.
Got someone to come and deliver bananas round the back of Waitrose?

indicators.note: going bananas means going crazy, so the letters of the word before are scrambled
round means placed so as to surround another piece
the back of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: taken as written before being rearranged
the last letter of Waitrose, a British supermarket chain

explanation.surface: A delivery driver hauling bananas round the back of a Waitrose supermarket.
explanation.walkthrough: Bananas looks like the cargo but is the shuffle signal. The definition is innocent on the surface, but also hints at relieving oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: To relieve a worker is to have a replacement come and take over their duty, so the person was relieved.

clue.text: Ring if stuck in Sir Tim's holes?

taken as written

explanation.surface: A smutty question about a famous lyricist's anatomy and where a ring might go.
explanation.definitionFit: Orifices are openings in the body, so holes is a plain synonym.

clue.text: Big noise behind Private Eye

the magazine speaks of itself as we, so it is us

explanation.surface: A loud fuss coming from somewhere behind the magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: A rumpus is a noisy disturbance or uproar, so it is a big noise.

clue.text: Leader chucked – alternative's misplaced

blocks.note: to cast is to throw or chuck
or introduces an alternative; the 's is short for is

explanation.surface: A leader has been thrown out because his replacement went missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Fidel Castro was the long-time leader of Cuba, so he is an example of a leader.

taken as written before rearrangement

explanation.definitionFit: Angola is a nation in south-west Africa, so it is an example of a country.

clue.text: Good to be covered in mushy gruel and make infantile sound

blocks.note: taken as written
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.definitionFit: A gurgle is the bubbling throaty noise a happy baby makes, so it is an infantile sound.

clue.text: Drippy wet, kissing Thatcher's butt, featured in Eye, possibly a growing thing

taken as written; it holds the other pieces
taken as written
the last letter of Thatcher, the former British prime minister

Jack with a French girl's top and a fur knotted peak

the first letter of girl
taken as written before rearrangement

blocks.note: the first and last letters of seducer
